name: Kenya RDM 1.3 (2025) - Cross-section elements
source: Republic of Kenya, Road Design Manual Volume 1: Geometric Design, Part 3: Geometric Design of Highways, Rural Roads and Urban Roads (2025), Chapter 4 Cross Section, S5.9-S5.10 and S12.9; Volume 2 Part 2 Drainage Design (2025) for drains.
advisory: Values are defaults and advisory checks only. Any value can be used; a value outside a range is reported as a departure (RDM 1.3 S1 departures from standards), never blocked.

references.cut_slope_by_height: Figure 4.15 (table of cut slope against height of cut)
references.superelevation: S5.9.2-S5.9.4, Table 5.7, S5.10; rates from the design review criteria (Tables 5.9-5.11)
references.drains: RDM 2.2 S6 (catch-water drains, mitre drains), S7.4.5.2 (150 mm freeboard)

lane.width.note: 3.65 m classes A, B; 3.50 m C, D; 3.25-3.50 m E; 3.00-3.50 m local roads; 3.75 m UA, UC; 3.00-3.50 m UL.

lane.crossfall.note: Bituminous rural roads 2.5 % minimum; gravel 4 %; earth 5 %.

shoulder.width.note: 2.7 m A, B; 2.0 m C; 1.5 m D; 1.0 m E and local; 1.0-1.5 m urban.

shoulder.crossfall.note: 4 % recommended; a sealed full-depth shoulder may follow the pavement with Chief Engineer approval; on superelevated sections both shoulders keep 4 %.

sidewalk.width.note: 1.5 m general low volume; 3.0 m or more for high pedestrian volumes; add 0.6 m when immediately next to the kerb (S4.5.1).

sidewalk.crossfall.note: Up to 5 % across accesses and driveways.

cycle_track.width.note: 2.0 m or more for high cyclist volumes.

median.width@raised.note: 2.5 m for a two-stage pedestrian refuge; 6.0 m for vehicle storage at crossings; 20 m recovery area.

median.width@flush.note: Non-restrictive: minimum 1 m (0.75 m at low flows and speeds).

kerb.height@barrier.note: Barrier kerbs should not normally be used above 70 km/h.

fill.slope.note: 1:4 or flatter is recoverable; 1:3-1:4 non-recoverable; steeper than 1:3 critical (consider a restraint system). Ratios here are horizontal per 1 vertical.

cut.backslope.note: Back slopes of 1:3 or flatter recommended within the clear zone.

side_drain.depth.note: 0.40 m minimum below formation for types A1-B3.

barrier.setback.note: 1.2 m verges without a sealed shoulder and medians; 0.6 m with a sealed shoulder; 0.6 m at 80 km/h and below.

slope_bands.ref: Table 4.20 (heights of slope in m; ratios horizontal per 1 vertical)

cut_by_height_fig_4_15.ref: Figure 4.15 (earth; 1:2 where earth is not stable at 1:1.5; rock 1:0.33 to 1:0.10)

A1.use: Hilly to mountainous terrain with heavy earthwork.

A2.use: Rolling terrain with moderate earthwork; flatter than A1 for capacity or velocity.

B1.use: Hilly terrain where a flatter ditch than A1 is needed.

B2.use: Rolling terrain where a flatter ditch than A2 is needed.

cutoff_2.use: Cut-off ditch type 2: large catchments, silting (Table 4.22).

cutoff_offset.note: Distance d from the edge of cutting to the cut-off ditch against height of cut.

widening.rule: Rows are [lowest radius, widening]: R >= 250 none; 120-250: 0.6; 60-120: 0.9; 40-60: 1.2; 20-40: 1.5 (two lanes). Below 20 m see S5.12 (hairpins).
widening.placement_ref: Table 4.15 note viii (inside of the curve)
widening.development_ref: Table 4.15 notes i, vi, vii (from the start of the transition, or over the runoff preceding the curve, to full width at the start of the circular curve)
widening.fill_ref: Table 4.15 fill widening, height measured from shoulder edge to toe; classes A to C

superelevation.rotation_ref: S5.9.2 (two-lane: centreline; dual carriageways often about the median edge)
superelevation.runoff_on_tangent_ref: S5.10: without transitions half the runoff on the straight; with a transition the runoff takes place within it
superelevation.shoulder_rule_ref: S4.4.3: on superelevated sections both shoulders keep 4 %

Carriageway.ref: Example only - enter the pavement design (RDM 3.4)

R4 single carriageway.ref: Table 4.23 R4: 1 x 3.65 m lane and 2.50 m shoulders each direction

R5 single carriageway.ref: Table 4.23 R5: 1 x 3.50 m lane and 2.00 m shoulders

R6 single carriageway.ref: Table 4.23 R6: 1 x 3.25 m lane and 1.50 m shoulders

R7 single carriageway.ref: Table 4.23 R7: 1 x 3.00 m lane and 1.00 m shoulders

R3 dual carriageway.ref: Table 4.23 R3: 2 x 3.65 m lanes, 2.70 m outer and 1.00 m inner shoulders, 2.00 m median each way

U5 urban single carriageway.ref: Table 4.24 U5: 1 x 3.50 m lane, 1.50 m shoulder, 2.00 m cycle track, 3.00 m walkway

U6 urban street.ref: Table 4.24 U6: 1 x 3.65 m lane, 3.50 m parking bay, 3.00 m raised walkway both sides

U4 urban dual carriageway.ref: Table 4.24 U4: 2 x 3.65 m lanes, 1.00 m inner and 2.00 m outer shoulder, 2.00 m median each way, raised walkway and cycle track

unsourced: Table 4.20 strong and weathered rock rows: the text layout does not show which value is fill, cut and back slope - confirm before adding.
Semi-mountable kerb dimensions: only in Figure 12.15 (SABS 927 types); defaults use 0.15 m high with a 1:1 face - confirm.
Relative gradient (Delta S max) for runoff: only in Figure 5.6; runoff uses Table 5.7, the 2-second rule and the spiral length.
Build-ups: the course stacks are examples; take the design from RDM 3.4 for the traffic class and subgrade.
